procedure: An independent session snapshots /admin/coord/home through the UI Bridge (text only), answers each question below using ONLY the page's text, and compares every answer with coord's project-state JSON read in the same minute (coord_project_state, or GET /coord/agent-project-state).
pass_rule: 10 of 10 answered. An answer of 'not measured / unknown, as of T' counts ONLY for a question whose block's door state is genuinely not 'read' in the compared JSON; the same words over a 'read' block are a miss. One miss means the metric reads 'no'.

questions.text: Does anything need me right now, and how many things?
questions.answer: The count of decisions waiting on the operator, equal to needs_me.total, with how many are shown and how many omitted; or 'nothing needs you' only when needs_me.total is 0.

questions.text: For the oldest item that needs me: what is the fork, what is recommended, what changes if I overturn it?
questions.answer: The first listed item's decision text, its recommendation (or the explicit 'open question — no recommendation'), and its if-overturned consequence (or 'not stated'), matching needs_me.items[0].

questions.text: Is any infrastructure degrading, and since when?
questions.answer: Each open degradation with its onset as observed by coord (absolute and relative time), matching degradations.open[].onset_observed_at; or 'nothing is degrading' only when degradations.headline is 'none'.

questions.text: Is that degradation being auto-remediated or waiting on someone?
questions.answer: Per open degradation, whether an agent response is bound to it, it waits on an operator, or it is a declared drain, matching auto_remediation / declared.

questions.text: How much of what the fleet says it verified survived independent checking?
questions.answer: The trust-calibration reading with its numerator and denominator; until a source exists, 'Not measured — no trust-calibration source'.

questions.text: Per repo: how much is shipped, in flight, stalled?
questions.answer: Per repo group, the shipped, in-flight and no-recorded-change counts, matching on_track.groups[].classes. The page words the 'stalled' class as 'no recorded change in N days'; that wording is the correct answer to 'stalled'.

questions.text: Which named pieces of work are stalled, and for how long?
questions.answer: The named units with no recorded change in the stall window and the time since their last recorded change, plus how many more were not named, matching on_track.groups[].named.stalled.

questions.text: What is the current initiative, when does it end, and how much in-flight work is attributed to it?
questions.answer: The initiative's in-scope items verbatim, its end date, and the attributed work — which reads 'not yet attributable' while on_track.initiative.alignment is 'unknown' (no declared link yet); that wording is a correct answer ONLY in that case.

questions.text: Which of the above can this page NOT currently tell me, and as of when was each source last read?
questions.answer: Every source the door lists, with its state and as-of time, matching does_not_know[]; the sources not read are exactly those whose state is not 'read'.
questions.unknown_is_an_answer_only_when: does_not_know is absent from the door's answer

questions.answer: Whether any merge-train degradation is open (a wedged train is one), matching degradations.open rows whose plane is merge_train, AND whether the merge-train watchers are fresh (the 'merge train:' line under Degrading, matching degradations.planes.merge_train.fresh / watchers). 'Nothing is degrading' answers it only when degradations.headline is 'none' and the merge-train line reads every watcher fresh.
